correctness.rationale: All distances are proved by intersection-orbit arguments; n=7 yields distinct-distance values 0,1,2,3 and bisector sizes 9,13,15. For n>=8, comparing three explicit orbit formulas isolates overlap two, whose minimum resolving-neighborhood cardinality is 2+2*C(n-4,2). For n=7 each of 21 switch pairs yields a unique largest failure with ten witness pairs; for n>=8 ground-point incidence frequencies 2, 1+C(n-4,2), 2(n-5) certify unique parametrization. Independent BFS and intersection-rule programs reproduce all values for n=7..11, but finite checks are not claimed to prove the theorem.

value.rationale: An infinite natural graph family receives a complete worst-case distance-sensing threshold and exact largest-failure multiplicities, including an exceptional odd-graph collapse from 210 optimal vertex-pair witnesses to 21 distinct bisectors. These are not implied by ordinary best-case metric dimension and provide a concrete structural benchmark for adversarial landmark placement and higher-rank Kneser questions.
